title: Chemical-product-name-disambiguation-notebook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for handling ambiguous spans where a token sequence could be either a chemical/active-ingredient, a brand/product name, or a colloquial shorthand. Mostly for ingestion into the next pass of our labeler guidelines and to capture weird examples we keep seeing in the dataset.

High-level problem framing:
- Many training docs contain short strings like "acetaminophen", "Tylenol", "Panadol", or "APAP". Same for industrial chemicals: "MEK" vs "methyl ethyl ketone" vs vendor product "MEK-Solve".
- Labeler instructions need deterministic fallbacks so adjudicators don't split on trivial preference. Right now we get disagreement between "INGREDIENT" vs "PRODUCT" on ~8% of samples in the medical subset.
- Downstream QA/enrichment (attribute mapping, safety filtering) depends on consistent canonicalization.

Quick heuristics (rough, test these):
1) Prefer EXPLICIT_BRAND if there's a trademark symbol or common brand token patterns: capitalized single-token brand followed by product class (e.g., "SteriWash disinfectant").
2) If name co-occurs with a dosage or concentration ("500mg", "0.5%") label as INGREDIENT/FORMULATION rather than PRODUCT unless brand context is explicit.
   - Rationale: doses usually attach to active ingredient mentions, e.g., "aspirin 81 mg" vs "Aspirin (Bayer) chewable".
3) Abbreviations (all-caps 2-4 letters) — try to resolve against a short acronym map. If acronym maps to a known chemical (APAP -> acetaminophen) label INGREDIENT and add alias metadata; if acronym looks like vendor shorthand (MEK-Solve) prefer PRODUCT.
4) Hyphenation and suffixes: tokens with vendor-style suffixes ("-X", "Pro", "Solv") -> PRODUCT. Noun phrases with generic class words (spray, cleaner, tablet) give strong PRODUCT signal.
5) Left/right context windows (±3 tokens): presence of verbs like "apply", "spray", "use" slightly biases PRODUCT. Presence of pharmacological verbs ("inhibits", "metabolized") biases INGREDIENT.
6) Chemical formulas and SMILES-like tokens -> INGREDIENT (e.g., "C6H6", "NaCl").

Examples to encode as test cases (annotate expected label):
- "Tylenol PM tablet" -> PRODUCT (brand + form)
- "acetaminophen 500 mg" -> INGREDIENT
- "APAP allergy noted" -> INGREDIENT (normalize APAP -> acetaminophen; tag alias)
- "MEK-Solve cleaner" -> PRODUCT
- "methyl ethyl ketone exposure" -> INGREDIENT/CHEMICAL
- "Panadol Rapid release" -> PRODUCT
- "chlorhexidine 0.12% rinse" -> INGREDIENT/FORMULATION
- "Bayer Aspirin chewable (81 mg)" -> PRODUCT (but also mark active ingredient aspirin)

Label structure proposal (fields to include in annotation CSV):
- span_text (string)
- label_class: INGREDIENT | PRODUCT | FORMULATION | UNKNOWN
- canonical_id: prefer public registry ID (RxNorm/CAS) when resolvable else vendor-id or free text
- alias_set: list of normalized aliases (lowercase)
- confidence_hint: manual|heuristic1|heuristic2 (for triage)

Open edge questions / TODOs:
- How aggressively do we auto-resolve acronyms? Risk: APAP -> acetaminophen is safe; but "PMS" could be product or condition. Need whitelist vs blacklist.
- Should we allow multi-labeling for spans that are both PRODUCT and INGREDIENT? (e.g., "Bayer Aspirin" -> PRODUCT primary, INGREDIENT secondary). That will break some downstream single-label pipelines. Maybe add secondary_label field instead.
- Decide canonical source for industrial chemicals: CAS registry vs internal dictionary; we need licensing for CAS? Check legal.
- Build a small mapping table for top ~500 high-frequency ambiguous tokens (Tylenol, aspirin, APAP, ibuprofen, MEK, Toluene, etc.). This should live in the labeling repo as "chemical_brand_map.json".

Adjudicator guidance (draft):
- If in doubt, choose the more specific label (PRODUCT if brand token present) and add a short adjudication note.
- Prefer to mark alias information even if label is PRODUCT so downstream resolution can still find active ingredient.

Mini action plan (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Extract top 2k spans from medical + industrial corpora where labeler disagreements > 20% (script: disagree_spans.py). Assign to pair adjudication. (Owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Draft small whitelist/blacklist for acronym auto-resolution (Owner: Maya).
- [ ] Add 200 curated test cases to evaluation harness and run baseline labeler to measure delta. (Owner: Rita)
- [ ] Quick sync with legal on CAS usage (Owner: Product-compliance) — add ticket JIRA-INV-2142.

Notes to self / random observations:
- We saw "Neosporin" used generically in user text to mean "any antibiotic ointment" — cultural/region signal matters. Possibly map to PRODUCT but keep alias set that includes generic phrase.
- Vendor product lines sometimes include the chemical name verbatim ("MEK premium") causing double-hit. Tooling should prefer PRODUCT if vendor tokens present.
- Rare OCR artifacts: spacing ("acet amo phen") — add normalization pass before labeling.

References and signals to surface in the labeling UI:
- show neighboring tokens, known registry matches (RxNorm/CAS), casing and punctuation cues, presence of dose/concentration, and known vendor-suffix dictionary.

Quick draft of short annotation help blurb for UI:
"Is the highlighted term referring to a brand/product or the active chemical/substance? If brand or product -> PRODUCT. If the mention is of the chemical itself (often comes with dose, formula, or pharmacological verb) -> INGREDIENT. If both apply, select PRODUCT and add the active ingredient in the secondary field."

End of scratchpad. Will fold into core labeling guidelines once we test heuristics and the 2-week actions complete.
